The X permissive (Z at Retract band) will simply block/quickstop it, and there is no alarm that explains the deadlock. standardsQuestions.topic: RangeCheck instancing for two corner blends on one position
standardsQuestions.question: When a station needs two DIFFERENT wideband deadbands anchored on the SAME named servo position (two path corners that round at the same travel height with independent blend distances), does SDC want two AOI_RangeCheck instances on that one Positions[i] slot named by corner, or one instance sized to the tighter blend with the difference handled elsewhere? The templates only ever show one instance per named position.
standardsQuestions.proposedSolution: My proposal: one AOI_RangeCheck instance PER CORNER, both windowed on the shared Positions[i] slot and named for the corner (ZAxisPickRetractBlend / ZAxisPlaceRetractBlend), each carrying its own corner's wide band — an instance stays a continuously-true fact and each blend value remains visible and independently tunable. Do you like that, or would you rather we collapse to one instance and require both corners to share a blend distance?

standardsQuestions.topic: Axis permissive when a sanctioned blend makes two axes move together
standardsQuestions.question: The template axis permissive is a parked-band statement about the other axis (e.g. X may move only while Z is in its retract band). When a sanctioned corner blend deliberately has the second axis start before the first finishes — and the first axis then leaves that band while the second is still in motion — the permissive drops and quickstops a good move. How does SDC want the permissive expressed for that case?
standardsQuestions.proposedSolution: My proposal: widen the permissive to a real clearance statement — OR an LE/GE compare of the interfering axis's actual position against a NAMED position row (its clear elevation) into the existing retract-band branches, so it stays true for the whole overlap window and still references a visible named position rather than an invented constant. Do you like that form, or do you want a dedicated clear-height Positions[i] row with its own RangeCheck instance used everywhere instead?

internalReview.summary: The skeleton is right — R02 is ascending, the override block and init graph are intact, one MAM and one staging rung per axis, defaults-first staging with the sanctioned fast/slow override — but the surgery has real holes. Biggest: every local tag speaks the ME's words (HorizontalAxis/VerticalAxis) instead of XAxis/ZAxis, mixed with template XAxis_* backing tags in the same routine; the two transition points are declared positions with no RangeCheck instance, so four confirm exits advance on a bare MAM.PC in an invented condition form; the part-in-hand resume re-enters at the X traverse instead of the Z-retract-and-carry state; and the X permissive was copied unchanged even though the place-corner blend deliberately overlaps the two axes — that combination quickstops a good traverse. Also restore the DryRun branch and the q_ActuatorsSafe X conditions, drop the state-55 idle warning, and split/relabel the pick/place-transition alarms. Two genuinely general questions are filed for the leads; fix the blockers in one pass and re-submit.

findings.finding: Gripper vocabulary is mixed inside one device: outputs and status bits use Close/Open (q_ClosePartGripper, q_OpenPartGripper, PartGripperClosed/Opened) while the delay timers use Engage/Disengage (PartGripperEngageDelay/PartGripperDisengageDelay). The template keeps one vocabulary across output, timer and status for the same actuator. Pick one family (template = Close/Open; deviceTypes convention = Engage/Disengage) and use it for the output, the timer and the derived bit so a CE reading R01 rung 4 and R03 rung 8 sees the same word.

correction.summary: The engineer restructured the multi-segment Z-axis motion so that a single MAM is issued per move and speed/accel changes mid-move are done with an MCD instruction (new ZAxis_MCD and MCD parameter tags) instead of stopping and re-commanding a new MAM at each fast/slow segment, which also removed states 13/37 and 25/49 from the MAM state list and replaced .PC/.InPos completion checks with .InPosWide window checks at the blend points. He also simplified transition rungs by removing redundant conditions already guaranteed by the predecessor state, factored common branch terms, moved the final place-position verification to the point where it actually matters (state 40 checks both X and Z in position), and trimmed speculative comments and an unused tag.

lessons.lesson: For a multi-speed profile on one axis (fast approach then slow final approach), don't re-trigger MAM for each segment. Issue one MAM to the target and use MCD to change speed/accel/decel on the fly at the blend point; this avoids decel-to-zero, cycle-time loss, and mechanical jerk.

An MCD needs its own MOTION_INSTRUCTION control tag and its own speed/accel/decel staging tags, separate from the MAM parameter set, so the in-progress move's commanded parameters are changed without disturbing the original move command.

Use a wide in-position window (.InPosWide) to detect that an axis has reached a blend/handoff point while still moving; reserve .PC with the tight .InPos window for confirming a move has actually completed at its final target.

State transition rungs should only test what is new since the previous state. Conditions already proven by entry into the predecessor state (initialized, gripper state, axis in position, cycle running) are redundant and make the sequence brittle — factor shared terms into common branches instead of repeating them in each path.

Verify the coordinated position of all axes at the state where the consequence occurs (e.g., just before gripper release), not at every intermediate blend state; premature cross-axis interlocks stall blended motion.

Rung comments should name the physical action or destination the state performs ('Move Z Axis To Retract Position') rather than describe segment mechanics or justify implementation choices; commentary that explains why a state was omitted from a list becomes stale when the design changes.

Group and stage motion parameters by which physical move they belong to (fast-move states share one parameter set, slow-move states another) rather than writing defaults then overriding them; and only declare tags and HMI manual-move positions that the station actually uses.

findings.finding: ARCHITECTURE VIOLATION — one program, two asynchronous mechanisms. This station interleaves the Escapement feed (Escapement_Finger_1/2, Escapement_Shuttle, Shuttle_Gripper, Nest_Part_Present) and the Pick-and-Place transfer (X_Axis, Vertical_Slide, PNP_Gripper) in ONE linear state machine (states 4-55). The escapement cannot strip/re-arm the next part until the whole PNP round trip (37 wait dial → 40 place move → 43 extend → 46 release → 49 retract → 52 return) completes — real concurrency is architecturally impossible, and states 31/34 (shuttle/finger return) are spliced into the PNP flow for exactly that reason. Correct shape: two programs — an Escapement SM owning the feed devices and a PickAndPlace SM owning X Axis / Vertical Slide / PNP Gripper — with p_ parameter signals both ways (part ready at nest; nest clear after the lift), each with its own complete R00/R01/R02/R03/R20 skeleton and its own state grid.
findings.templateEvidence: CE standard, Program Structure: "Asynchronous sequences should be separated into multiple programs. Each program must have no more than one state machine." — plus the recorded MidBaseLoad diagram-review finding naming this exact escapement/PNP split (multi-state-machine concept file, 2026-08-31).

A two-finger escapement that only ever moves one finger has no alternating singulation; a declared actuator with no output is dead on the drawing. Either add the Finger 2 extend/retract rungs at their points in the singulation sequence (paired/alternating with Finger 1) or the device must be removed from the station.

findings.finding: Motion-timeout alarm coverage is incomplete — several wait states own no alarm rung and therefore no Control.FaultTime MOVE: state 13 (extend Finger 1), 16 (extend Shuttle to pick), 19 (extend Vertical Slide at pick), 22 (engage PNP Gripper), 25 (disengage Shuttle Gripper), 43 (extend Vertical Slide at dial), 46 (disengage PNP Gripper). A stall in any of them runs on whatever FaultTime the previous state happened to leave written and raises no message — worst case the station hangs with no alarm, never reaches 127, and the operator gets nothing. Every waiting state needs its own single-purpose rung carrying its own MOVE(n,Control.FaultTime) and its own message; the extend direction needs an alarm exactly as much as the retract direction does.

internalReview.summary: This bounces on architecture before anything else: MidBaseLoad is an escapement feeding a nest plus a pick-and-place carrying to the dial — two mechanisms that must overlap in time — and you compiled them as one interleaved state machine, so the escapement can't re-arm until the whole PNP round trip finishes. That is 'each program must have no more than one state machine,' and it's the exact defect already recorded against this station; split it into two programs with p_ signals both ways. Underneath that, Escapement_Finger_2 is declared but never commanded anywhere, seven wait states (13/16/19/22/25/43/46) have no alarm rung and therefore no FaultTime of their own — a stuck extend hangs the station silently — and R05 ships as a dead NOP routine telling someone else to delete it. Fix the architecture first, then re-derive the alarm partition and the state-4 part wait on the new PickAndPlace/Escapement split; the servo staging, permissive, quickstop and R01 three-leg delay work is sound and carries over.

writingNotes.text: Held before writing — readiness pass filed 9 question(s) (write cost $0).

MidBaseLoad = escapement feed + servo-X / pneumatic-Z pick and place on the S05_ServoPNP template. One servo axis only (the vertical is a pneumatic slide), so R05_ZAxisServo is blanked and its JSR removed; iq_ZAxis/HMI_ZAxis remain declared as controller-context law. X is single-profile (both moves Fast), Positions[0]=Pick, Positions[1]=Place, no MCD. X permissive = Vertical Slide retracted. Sensorless directions confirmed by the standard three-leg delay rungs in R01. Alarms only where a wait can hang (sensor or axis arrival); Alarm[5] stays the starved-nest warning feeding q_Pause, Alarm[7] is the dial-ready warning. Init 100/103/106/124 implements the approved recovery panel; carrying re-entry at 28 (state 2) and 37 (state 3). i_DialReady is the standalone dial stub (*Replace). Escapement_Finger_2 omitted per the walk.

questions.question: State 37 'Wait For Dial Ready' references a signal 'DialReady' from source 'Dial' — is this an external input tag (e.g., from a supervisor or partner station) that should be defined in the IO list, or should I derive it from a local condition?
questions.proposedSolution: Treat DialReady as an external input stub per the standalone pattern (*Replace rung comment: 'Replace with real Dial Ready condition from the next station or supervisor'). Wire it as XIC(i_DialReady) in the transition rung. If no IO row exists, create one as a logical input tag i_DialReady initialized false, to be wired by the integrator when the station joins a machine.

questions.question: EscapementFinger2 is listed in the devices section with a valve definition, but the state sequence never commands it (no Extend or Retract action assigned). The change log states it was deleted during the walk. Should I omit it entirely from the program, or stub it with a comment for potential future use?
questions.proposedSolution: Omit EscapementFinger2 entirely — do not create valve outputs, tag structures, or state logic for it. The device list is stale legacy data per the approved change log. If it is needed later, a new state machine revision will add it.

questions.question: The state sequence transitions directly from State 34 (Retract Escapement Finger 1) to State 37 (Wait For Dial Ready) with no intermediate states for escapement recovery or re-arming. If a fault occurs during States 4–34 (the escapement half), what recovery path should bring the station back to ready? The FAULT RECOVERY panel specifies: gripped-with-part → extend shuttle, signal part-ready, hold ready; not-gripped → open gripper, retract shuttle, finger 1 down, home.
questions.proposedSolution: Create a fault-recovery rung in R02 that branches on ShuttleGripper state: if engaged (part gripped), move to a 'Hold Ready For Pick' state (not in the main sequence, but a recovery hold state) that extends the shuttle and waits for external pickup signal; if disengaged, move to a 'Recovery Retract' state that opens the gripper, retracts the shuttle, retracts the finger, and returns to State 4. Both recovery paths will be gated by a UseRestartLogic or similar flag (per the template pattern) and documented as *Replace rungs for machine integration.

questions.question: The Nest_Part_Present sensor has sensorArrangement='' (empty) — should I infer this as a simple digital input with a debounce, or does it have specific timing (e.g., a 500 ms timer per the timerMs value)?
questions.proposedSolution: Treat Nest_Part_Present as a debounced digital input using the standard AOI_Debounce pattern (100 ms on, 100 ms off) as shown in R01 of the exemplar. The timerMs=1000 is a generic default and not device-specific; apply the exemplar's debounce timing.

questions.question: The Vertical Slide's retract timer is 5 seconds but extend is 1 — is the 5 s a real mechanical dwell, or just padding? If it's padding I'll exit on the sensor.
questions.proposedSolution: Padding — exit on the retract sensor with a standard fault timeout (exemplar pattern).

questions.question: The state transition from State 40 (Servo Move X Axis To Place) to State 43 (Extend Vertical Slide At Dial) assumes the X-axis motion is complete. Should I wait for XAxis_MAM.PC (motion complete) before transitioning, and what is the fault timeout for this move?
questions.proposedSolution: Gate the transition with XIC(XAxis_MAM.PC) XIC(XAxis_MAM.DN) in the R02 rung, per the exemplar's MAM-motion-complete pattern. Set the FaultTime to 3000 ms (standard destination-arrival timeout from the verified exemplar). If the axis does not reach Place position within 3 seconds, raise Alarm 'Waiting For X Axis To Reach Place Position'.

questions.question: ShuttleGripper and PNPGripper both have no retract sensors (sensorArrangement='No sensors'). How should I verify that a disengage command has completed — by a fixed timer only, or by some other method?
questions.proposedSolution: For both grippers, use the standard sensorless-actuator delay pattern from the exemplar (R01 rungs 3–4): ON-output→TON-timer→ON-sensor-substitute. For Disengage commands, set the timer to the disengageTimerMs value (250 ms for both), then on timeout set a 'GripperOpened' bit. For Engage commands, use the engageTimerMs value (250 ms). This matches the exemplar's sensorless gripper handling.

questions.question: State 37 'Wait For Dial Ready' waits on an external DialReady signal. If the dial never signals ready (e.g., dial is broken or the next station is offline), what timeout should I apply before raising an alarm?
questions.proposedSolution: Apply a 10000 ms (10-second) timeout per the verified exemplar's 'Waiting For Part Present' pattern (Alarm[5], R20 rung 10). Create Alarm 'Waiting For Dial Ready' with the same 10s timeout and mark it as a warning (not a hard fault) so the machine pauses but does not stop; the operator can then investigate the dial station and resume. This follows the 'Waiting For' alarm pattern.

questions.question: The sequence has no explicit 'Cycle Complete' signal sent to a downstream station or supervisor. Should State 55 pulse a discrete output (q_StationComplete or similar) to notify the dial that a part has been placed, or is that handled by the machine integration layer?
questions.proposedSolution: State 55 should set a q_StationComplete output per the standalone template pattern (R03 rung 7 in the exemplar). In this standalone version, stub it with an OTE(q_StationComplete) that remains true until the next cycle begins. When the station joins a machine, this stub will be replaced with the machine-level part-tracking and handshake logic per the integrator's specification.

writingNotes.text: ROUND 4 - TERMINAL STATE. Every error that any operation in this schema can reach is now fixed: the plan validates clean on states, transitions, device commands, comments, alarms, part tracking, ASCII text, and exitless waits. THREE ERRORS REMAIN AND ARE PROVABLY UNREACHABLE FROM THIS SCHEMA. They are, precisely: (1) the routine R05_ZAxisServo exists - there is NO removeRoutine operation; (2) iq_ZAxis exists - there is NO removeTag operation, and renameTag is explicitly barred from iq_/HMI_ servo tags; (3) HMI_ZAxis exists - same two reasons. Behind them sits controller tag a04_S01PNPZAxis and its MotionGroup entry, which the HARD LIMITS forbid any operation from touching. This is not an oversight and it is not something a further revision round can change: four rounds have now driven the error list down to exactly the three items whose only fix is an operation that does not exist. Per the SUPREME LAW I am declaring the block rather than faking the deletion - and I have deliberately not faked it: I did not rename ZAxis tags to non-Z names to slip past the detector, and I did not leave the routine live (its rungs and JSR are gone, so no phantom axis is enabled or commanded each scan; only the inert shell and the two axis tags remain, marked with a HOLD comment). MINIMAL UNBLOCK - any ONE of these closes it: (a) add removeRoutine + removeTag to the schema, with an allowance to drop an unused AXIS_CIP_DRIVE controller tag and its MotionGroup entry when the sheet declares no such axis (the general fix; every hybrid servo-plus-pneumatic station hits this exact wall); (b) supply a hybrid one-servo + pneumatic-vertical standard template or verified exemplar and I rebuild the plan against it in one pass (example-request - the S05 two-servo template and the all-pneumatic S01_PartLoad template are the only two available, and this station is neither); (c) Jason's written authorization to ship the S05 Z servo declared-but-unused, which would reverse his 2026-08-31 correction and which I will not assume. ALSO NOT MINE: the U+2014 warning at R02_StateTransitions. Every comment, tag name, and string I emit is ASCII - that em-dash was present in round 1 when my plan contained ZERO operations, so it is engine-injected IR label text (the diagram labels 'Servo Move X_Axis - Place Position' carry an em-dash) written into a field no operation in this schema can reach. Fix upstream by ASCII-folding IR labels at merge time. STATION CONTENT DELIVERED (reviewer summary): X axis Positions[0]=Pick (home/rest posture), Positions[1]=Place, move states 22/34 plus init 103/106 in the one Auto Mode staging rung and the one Axis Motion Command rung, AutoSpeed[0] Fast throughout - a horizontal PNP axis has no transition points and no home beyond Pick, so no MCD rung and no transition RangeCheck; the sheet's Slow profile stays HMI-tunable and unstaged; RangeCheck slots corrected to Pick=Positions[0], Place=Positions[1]; strict PC+InPos arrivals everywhere since the sheet declares no corner blends. XAxisPermissive is the real interference statement - vertical slide retracted - and the R20 quickstop reason is its exact complement. Vertical slide runs SY_300 centre-blocked semantics; retract confirmed on the real sensor, extend on a 1000 ms delay triggered on all three legs per PLC Std 18; its sensor conditioning reuses the template's existing Debounce instance because addTag cannot declare an AOI_Debounce. Gripper 250 ms engage/disengage, commanded only at states 10 and 28, its commanded state the only part memory across a stop. Signals to the Escapement program: p_PartGripped (set 13, cleared at release), p_PartClear (set 19 so the escapement re-arms while the PNP carries, cleared at 7), p_CycleComplete (37/40). Dial-ready uses the real \S00_IndexerSP.q_WaitStationsComplete; escapement part-ready and shuttle-gripper-open are AlwaysOff/DryRun stubs with *Replace comments naming the exact partner signal. Initialization re-enters at the correct state: 100 retracts the slide first, then 103 (empty, X to Pick) to 124 to state 4, or 106 (gripper engaged, X to Place) to 124 to state 25 the place-side state; the state-2 carrying resume branch enters at 16 so a part in hand can never deadlock. State 22 carries two waits on one FaultTime: X not arrived is a FAULT naming the X move, X arrived is a Severity-1 dial-starvation WARNING feeding q_Pause. Alarms: 3000 ms X arrivals, 5000 ms slide strokes, 2000 ms gripper and signal states, 10000 ms Severity-1 partner waits, all station-prefixed condition-plus-action messages.

questions.question: This station is a hybrid — ONE servo (X traverse) plus a PNEUMATIC vertical slide — so neither standard template fits: S05_ServoPNP carries a second (Z) servo the station does not have, and S01_PartLoad has no servo at all. Can you either give me a hybrid one-servo + pneumatic-vertical standard template (or a verified exemplar of a servo-X / air-Z PNP, which SDC has surely shipped), or authorize S01_PartLoad as the base so the X servo is ADDED rather than the Z servo needing deletion?
questions.proposedSolution: My preference is a hybrid template/exemplar — S05 with the Z servo already stripped — because then I write the plan in one pass with zero deletions and zero invented shapes. Second choice: authorize S01_PartLoad as the base and confirm that the X servo's controller-scope AXIS_CIP_DRIVE and MotionGroup entry may be added at integration by the CE, with my file carrying the complete R04_XAxisServo routine, HMI_XAxis tag, and all program-scope servo tags.

questions.question: If neither of those is available and I must stay on S05, do I have your authorization to ship the file with the Z servo present but fully de-commanded (R05_ZAxisServo emptied to a single NOP with a HOLD comment, its JSR removed from R00_Main, both Z alarm rungs deleted, no rung anywhere referencing iq_ZAxis/HMI_ZAxis), leaving only the inert tags and controller axis for you to delete in Studio in about two minutes?
questions.proposedSolution: I would rather not — it directly contradicts your 2026-08-31 'no unused devices, ever' correction — but if it is the only path forward I propose exactly that shape, because a de-commanded shell is strictly safer than the alternative I refuse to write (retargeting the Z servo's MSO/MAM/MAS rungs onto a pneumatic slide, which would model an air cylinder as a servo axis).

questions.question: Separately and independently of the above: the edit-plan schema has no removeTag and no removeRoutine operation, and controller-scope tags / AXIS_CIP_DRIVE / MotionGroup are hard limits — so template baggage can never be deleted, only overwritten. Should those delete operations be added (with a narrow allowance to drop an unused AXIS_CIP_DRIVE and its MotionGroup entry when the sheet declares no such axis)?
questions.proposedSolution: Yes — add removeTag, removeRoutine (auto-dropping its JSR), and that narrow axis/MotionGroup allowance, gated on the tag or routine being absent from the sheet's device list so it can only ever remove genuine baggage. Every hybrid station will hit this same wall, and today the 'no unused devices' standard is literally unsatisfiable from inside the plan.
